{{short description|On certain subgroups of a minimal simple finite group of odd order}}
In mathematical [[finite group]] theory, Thompson's original '''uniqueness theorem''' {{harv|Feit|Thompson|1963|loc= theorems 24.5 and 25.2}} states that in a minimal [[simple group|simple]] finite [[group (mathematics)|group]] of odd [[order (group theory)|order]] there is a unique maximal [[subgroup]] containing a given [[elementary abelian group|elementary abelian subgroup]] of [[Rank of a group|rank]]&nbsp;3. {{harvtxt|Bender|1970}} gave a shorter proof of the uniqueness theorem.
